CLINICAL BACKGROUND

  • The NRAS proto-oncogene encodes a GTPase that functions in signal transduction and is a member of the RAS superfamily which also includes KRAS and HRAS.
  • RAS proteins mediate the transmission of growth signals from the cell surface to the nucleus via the PI3K/AKT/MTOR and RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathways, which regulate cell division, differentiation, and survival.
  • Recurrent mutations in RAS oncogenes cause constitutive activation and are found in 20-30% of cancers. NRAS mutations are particularly common in melanomas (up to 25%) and are observed at frequencies of 5-10% in acute myeloid leukemia, colorectal, and thyroid cancers.
  • The majority of NRAS mutations consist of point mutations at G12, G13, and Q61. Mutations at A59, K117, and A146 have also been observed but are less frequent.

POTENTIAL RELEVANCE

  • Currently, no therapies are approved for NRAS aberrations.
  • The EGFR antagonists, cetuximab and panitumumab, are contraindicated for treatment of colorectal cancer patients with NRAS mutations in exon 2 (codons 12 and 13), exon 3 (codons 59 and 61), and exon 4 (codons 117 and 146).

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

METHODOLGY: REAL-TIME PCR: The RAS Mutation Panel is a PCR based assay that uses allele‐specific primers in a multiplex reaction to identify the presence of the mutations in a total of 8 reactions per sample. Exons 2, 3 and 4 of KRAS & NRAS genes are screened for the presence of Mutations as shown in the Table. The test identifies but does not distinguish between mutations within each group.

LIMITATIONS AND DISCLAIMERS:

The analytical sensitivity of the test allows detection of the mutation when the mutant clone comprises at least 5% of the total genomic DNA. Tumor sample must be fixed under appropriate conditions (10% Neutral buffered formalin for 24‐72hrs) to ensure preservation of amplifiable quality DNA. PCR is a highly sensitive technique; reasons for apparently contradictory results may be due to improper quality control during sample collection and fixation, high degree of necrosis, mucin content and/or presence of PCR inhibitors.
